elements.element: No minimum purchase commitment applies to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 states that Customer commits to purchase “no minimum amount of Services.” The vestigial three-year reference does not impose a positive minimum.

elements.element: Customer pays fees only for Services ordered or used.
Any minimum purchase commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: The clause does not impose any minimum purchase commitment, so the condition under which a commitment would need a 12-month limit is demonstrably absent. The retained three-year wording applies to a zero minimum.

elements.element: Customer may reduce any minimum purchase commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: No minimum commitment exists, so there is no commitment requiring a reduction mechanism. Although the clause mentions reduction rights, it does not specify 30 days' notice; the element is met only because its triggering commitment is absent.

elements.element: Any commitment shortfall is addressed through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Because there is no minimum commitment and Customer pays only for Services ordered or used, no commitment shortfall or associated penalty can arise. Express true-up language is therefore unnecessary under the rendered position.

result.reason: The operative language achieves the preferred position and therefore also satisfies the conditional fallback protections by eliminating any positive commitment. It is not minimal because “with reduction or termination rights” is unnecessary once the minimum is eliminated, and it is imprecise because those rights have no stated scope or mechanics. The phrases “commits to purchase no minimum amount” and “in each of the next three years” are also awkward vestiges, although they do not create a positive purchase obligation. The unrelated order-of-precedence provision remains unchanged.
